This Petition Is Filed Under Section 482 Of Cr.P.C
Praying To Quash The Private Complaint In
Pcr.No.25/2019 On The File Of The Principal Senior
Civil Judge And C.J.M., Mangalore Presented For The
Offence P/U/S 406, 417, 418, 420, 506 Of Ipc.
 This Petition Coming On For Orders, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

Respondent No.2 filed a private complaint under Section 200 Cr.P.C. for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 417, 418, 420 and 506 of IPC alleging that, respondent No.2 and his wife were running a partnership business in the name and style of 'Saanvi Automobiles'.
Since there was difficulty in carrying on the business of the firm, five persons were inducted as partners on 04.10.2017 by executing a Deed of Reconstitution of the Partnership.

However, the newly inducted persons failed to run the business in terms of the Reconstitution Deed and accused No.1 who is an advocate by profession and was offering legal advise to the complainant, had undertaken to settle the matter, and in the process prepared a deed dated 04.10.2018 showing himself and the petitioners as partners in the business and a separate Memorandum of Understanding was signed by all the parties wherein, the said advocate and the petitioners have undertaken to close the overdraft facility availed by the complainant as against the running stock of the firm.

2. It was further alleged that, Mr. K.S.N.Rajesh though started managing the affairs of the business of the firm, failed to pay the rentals to the landlord and close the overdraft facility availed by the complainant and also failed to pay the agreed 5% profit in the business to the complainant.

3. The learned Magistrate referred the complaint to the police for investigation under Section 156(3)
of Cr.P.C.
Taking exception of the same, accused Nos.2 & 3 are before this Court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the order passed by the learned Magistrate referring the complaint to the police for investigation under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. is one without due process of law, since the complaint was filed without complying with the mandatory provisions contained in Sections 154(1) & 154(3) of Cr.P.C.

He further submits that since there was dispute between the parties, the accused had raised dispute and the sole arbitrator has passed an award dated 10.02.2020 directing respondent No.2-complainant to pay a sum of Rs.29,69,472/-.

Hence,
he submits that the dispute between the parties arises out of alleged breach of conditions of the deed of reconstitution of the firm, however, given a criminal texture so as to wreak vengeance against the petitioner-accused and with revengeful intent.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent would submit that the allegation made in the complaint clearly discloses the cognizable offences and the learned Magistrate has rightly passed the impugned order and the veracity of the allegations requires to be investigated, and at this stage, the impugned order passed by the learned Magistrate does not warrant any interference.
6.
I have examined the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.
7. Perusal of the complaint and the award passed by the sole arbitrator indicates that there is a dispute with regard to the management of the Partnership Firm.
The sole arbitrator has passed an award directing respondent No.2 to pay the amount invested by the accused - petitioner including damages.

This clearly indicates that dispute between the parties arises out of the alleged breach of conditions contained in the deed of reconstitution, however, given a criminal texture so as to wreck vengeance i.e., the petitioner- accused and with revengeful intent so as to pressurize the petitioners-accused to arrive at the settlement.
8. The perusal of the complaint also indicates that respondent No.2 before filing the private complaint had not approached the police to register the FIR against the petitioners-accused.
The offences alleged against petitioners- accused are cognizable.

The complaint filed without complying sections 154(1) & 154(3) of Cr.P.C. is not maintainable as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of PRIYANKA SRIVASTAVA VS. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH AND OTHERS reported in (2015) 6 SCC 287.

entities.text: PRIYANKA SRIVASTAVA VS. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH AND OTHERS reported in (2015) 6 SCC 287
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, continuation of the investigation by the police will be an abuse of process of law, since the probability of the police laying a charge sheet is unlikely since the dispute between the parties which is purely civil in nature.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. Criminal petition is allowed.
ii. The impugned proceedings in PCR No.25/2019 on the file of Principal Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Mangalore, is hereby quashed insofar as it relates to accused Nos.2 & 3.
As the main matter is disposed of, pending I.As. does not survive for consideration.
